title: Ordinary uncurrying represents the derived transpose on one-K-flat pairs
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $U,V,I$ be arbitrary cochain complexes of $R$-modules, with localization $Q$ to $D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Use product total Hom [def-sc-module-total-hom-complex] and direct-sum total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Assume $I$ is K-injective [def-pur-kinjective-complex], and assume at least one of $U,V$ is K-flat [def-pc-module-kflat-complex]. Give $D(R)$ the canonical closed symmetric monoidal structure [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal]. Let
$$c_{U,V}:Q\operatorname{Tot}(U\otimes_RV)\xrightarrow{\sim}QU\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}QV$$
be the natural one-K-flat comparison induced by the inverse localization tensorator [lem-sf-ringed-derived-native-tensor], and let
$$j_{V,I}:Q\operatorname{Hom}_R^\bullet(V,I)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\operatorname{Hom}_R(QV,QI)$$
be the canonical K-injective representative comparison [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Suppose $\phi:U\to\operatorname{Hom}_R^\bullet(V,I)$ and $\psi:\operatorname{Tot}(U\otimes_RV)\to I$ are chain maps such that $\psi(u\otimes v)=\phi(u)(v)$ for all homogeneous $u\in U^p$, $v\in V^q$, interpreted through the actual Hom product projections. Then their localizations satisfy
$$\operatorname{tr}_{QU,QV,QI}\bigl(Q(\psi)\circ c_{U,V}^{-1}\bigr)=j_{V,I}\circ Q(\phi),$$
where $\operatorname{tr}$ is the right-tensor adjunction bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(QU\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}QV,QI)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(QU,R\operatorname{Hom}_R(QV,QI))$. There is no boundedness, finite-generation or degreewise-flatness assumption.

source.place: Tag 0A65 (lemma-internal-hom), proof and equation-internal-hom: compatibility of the derived adjunction with ordinary tensor-Hom uncurrying. The one-K-flat representative formulation is extracted from this construction.

proof.text: Work on the terminal one-object site with coefficient ring $R$: module sheaves are $R$-modules, and sheaf tensor and product Hom are the actual module constructions. By [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] choose a quasi-isomorphism $q:P\to V$ with $P$ K-flat and all terms flat; also choose $a:F\to U$ with $F$ K-flat with flat terms. No boundedness of either resolution is required. Write $T(X,Y)=\operatorname{Tot}(X\otimes_RY)$ and $h=Qq$. Localization makes $h$ and $Qa$ isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution), applied on the terminal site.

proof.text: Let $s=\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}(q,I)$ be precomposition, put $\phi_P=s\circ\phi$, and put $t=T(1_U,q)$ and $\psi_P=\psi\circ t$. These are chain maps by functoriality of product Hom and total tensor. For $u\in U^p$ and $z\in P^q$, actual product projections give $\phi_P(u)(z)=\phi(u)(qz)=\psi(u\otimes qz)=\psi_P(u\otimes z)$. Equality on each pure-tensor summand determines a map out of $T(U,P)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-module-tensor-hom-currying] and the direct-sum universal property. Thus $\psi_P$ is exactly the ordinary uncurrying of $\phi_P$, with no factor interchange or extra sign.

source.place: Tag 0A65 (lemma-internal-hom), proof and equation-internal-hom; agent extension to one-K-flat representatives by naturality.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sfb-hom-kflat-chain-transpose] with $A=U$, $P=P$, $E=I$, for the closed structure $S$ of $\operatorname{tr}$ and its K-flat models $T$. Its flat-term hypothesis holds for $P$, and its K-injective hypothesis is exactly the assumption on $I$. By [lem-sf-ringed-derived-tensor-hom-adjunction] the closed structure of $\operatorname{tr}$ has the native monoidal structure and its K-flat models $T$ are the native simultaneous K-flat comparison; so on the K-flat pair $(F,P)$ the comparison $c^*_{F,P}$ of the theorem is $T(F,P)=c_{F,P}$. Its comparison $c^*_{U,P}$ agrees with inversion of the representative quasi-isomorphism $T(a,1_P)$, and the native comparison is natural [lem-sf-ringed-derived-native-tensor]; for $a:F\to U$ from step 1 both therefore satisfy $c_{U,P}\circ Q(T(a,1_P))=(Qa\otimes1)\circ c_{F,P}$ with the same right side. The map $T(a,1_P)$ is a quasi-isomorphism since $P$ is K-flat [def-pc-module-kflat-complex], so its localization cancels and $c^*_{U,P}=c_{U,P}$. The Hom comparison in that theorem is the fixed augmentation $I\to I(I)$ followed by the derived-Hom representative identification, hence is $j_{P,I}$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. The pure-tensor equality in step 2 says that $\psi_P$ is the chain map $\widetilde{\phi_P}$ of that theorem, which therefore yields
$$\operatorname{tr}_{QU,QP,QI}\bigl(Q\psi_P\circ c_{U,P}^{-1}\bigr)=j_{P,I}\circ Q\phi_P.$$

source.place: Tag 0A65 (lemma-internal-hom), proof and equation-internal-hom; agent extension to one-K-flat representatives by naturality.

proof.text:
Set $A=Q\psi\circ c_{U,V}^{-1}$, $B=j_{V,I}\circ Q\phi$, and $H=R\operatorname{Hom}_R(h,1_{QI})$. Both $c_{U,P}$ and $c_{U,V}$ are invertible: the former because $P$ is K-flat and the latter by the given one-K-flat hypothesis. Naturality of the native comparison gives
$$c_{U,V}\circ Qt=(1_{QU}\otimes h)\circ c_{U,P},\qquad Q\psi_P\circ c_{U,P}^{-1}=A\circ(1_{QU}\otimes h).$$
For the Hom representative comparison, functoriality of the localized product Hom gives
$$j_{P,I}\circ Qs=H\circ j_{V,I},\qquad j_{P,I}\circ Q\phi_P=H\circ B.$$
Here precomposition by $q$ really is a quasi-isomorphism on Hom representatives: apply [lem-pur-rhom-well-defined] with target map $1_I$ between K-injectives and source map $q$. Thus the displayed comparison is the canonical localized one, and uses no flatness assumption on $V$ or on individual terms of $U$.

source.place: Tag 0A65 (lemma-internal-hom), proof and equation-internal-hom; agent extension to one-K-flat representatives by naturality.

proof.text:
Naturality in the second variable of the canonical right-tensor adjunction [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal] says
$$\operatorname{tr}_{QU,QP,QI}\bigl(A\circ(1_{QU}\otimes h)\bigr)=H\circ\operatorname{tr}_{QU,QV,QI}(A).$$
Substitute both identities of step 4 into step 3 to obtain $H\circ\operatorname{tr}(A)=H\circ B$. The derived internal Hom is a functor, so $H$ is invertible with inverse $R\operatorname{Hom}_R(h^{-1},1_{QI})$; composing on the left with this inverse gives $\operatorname{tr}(A)=B$, precisely the asserted equality. This argument handles either K-flat factor without changing the tensor order.
